title: Pizza Diavola
subtitle: Spicy salami and chilli pizza
excerpt: Pizza Diavola is a spicy pizza topped with tomato, mozzarella, sliced spicy salami, and dried chilli flakes. The fat from the salami renders into the cheese as it bakes, making it rich and slightly oily in the best possible way.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Prepare the dough 24 hours ahead. The topping goes on just before baking.
recipe.temperatureNote: Fan or conventional, maximum oven setting. Preheat for at least 45 minutes with a heavy tray or pizza stone inside.

content.text: Pizza Diavola is a tomato and mozzarella pizza with sliced spicy salami and chilli flakes. It is one of the most popular pizzas outside Naples for a good reason: the salami crisps at the edges in a hot oven, the fat spreads into the mozzarella, and the chilli cuts through the richness. If you want heat, this is the pizza to make.
You need one 210 g ball of 24-hour pizza dough per pizza, rested at room temperature for 2 hours before shaping.

items.prepNote: use a spicy cured salami if available; prosciutto with extra chilli also works

content.text: Heat the oven to its maximum setting with a heavy tray or pizza stone on the top shelf. Preheat for at least 45 minutes.
Season the passata with salt and stir. Drain and tear the mozzarella.
Stretch one dough ball to a rough 30 cm disc, leaving a 2 cm border.
Spread the passata over the disc. Scatter the mozzarella, then lay the salami slices over the top. Sprinkle with chilli flakes and drizzle with olive oil.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes until the rim is charred and the salami is slightly crisp at the edges. Eat immediately.

The name diavola means devil, which is a reference to the heat from the chilli and the fiery red of the spicy salami. It is not a single fixed recipe but a type: any pizza with cured spicy pork and heat qualifies. The version here uses prosciutto or another cured pork slice alongside a good pinch of dried chilli, which gives the same result without needing a specific cut.
